title: Functions
description: def, parameters, return values, and closures

exercises.title: Basic Function
exercises.description: Create a function greet() that Console.WriteLines Hello. Call it in main.
hints: Declare `static void Greet()` and call it directly from top-level/Main context.

exercises.title: Function with Parameters
exercises.description: Create function greet(name string) that Console.WriteLines Hello, name. Call with "Alice".
hints: Parameter type is `string` with **PascalCase** naming by convention.
exercises.solution:
Greet("Alice");

static void Greet(string name) { Console.WriteLine($"Hello, {name}"); }

exercises.title: Function with Return
exercises.description: Create function add(a, b int) int that returns a+b. Call with 3 and 4, Console.WriteLine result.
exercises.starter_code:
// Console.WriteLine(Add(3, 4));

static int Add(int a, int b) => 0;
hints: Return `int` from `Add(int a, int b)` expression-bodied method.
exercises.solution:
Console.WriteLine(Add(3, 4));

static int Add(int a, int b) => a + b;

exercises.title: Multiple Return Values
exercises.description: Create function divide(a, b int) (int, error) that returns quotient and nil error, or 0 and error if b is 0. Call with 10 and 3, Console.WriteLine result and error.
exercises.starter_code:
// print Divide(10,3) and nil for Divide(10,0)

static int? Divide(int a, int b) => null;
hints: Model missing-quotient scenarios with nullable `int?` when denominators vanish.
Print `<nil>` exactly when the checker expects that literal sentinel text.
Separate successful division from the zero division path before formatting output.

exercises.title: Variadic Function
exercises.description: Create function sum(numbers ...int) int that sums all numbers. Call with 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and Console.WriteLine the result.
exercises.starter_code:
// Console.WriteLine(Sum(1,2,3,4,5));

static int Sum(params int[] nums) => 0;
hints: Mark the final parameter `params int[] nums` so callers pass arbitrary arity.
Sum with LINQ `.Sum()`, a `foreach`, or accumulator loop.

exercises.title: Defer Statement
exercises.description: Create a function process() that Console.WriteLines "start", defers Console.WriteLineing "end", and Console.WriteLines "working". Call it in main.
exercises.starter_code:
// Process();

static void Process() { /* start, working, defer end */ }
hints: Order side effects explicitly: start → working → end on separate lines.
Use `try` / `finally` if you want cleanup that always runs.

exercises.title: Closure
exercises.description: Create function makeAdder() that returns a function that adds to a running total. Create adder = makeAdder(), then call adder(5) and adder(10), Console.WriteLineing both results.
hints: Return `Func<int, int>` that closes over mutable local state.
Each invocation should update the accumulator before returning.
